correction.text: Zabulistan around Ghazni with the Arachosian land (Bost) shown in Cliopatria's 682 shape, the kingdom of Rutbil after he 'split from his brother, the Shahi of Kabul' (680-683)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 680-691: Rutbil ruled 'Zabulistan, around Ghazni' and, by the 673 treaty, held 'Kabul and Zabul'; Arachosia 'as far as Kandahar' is Turk Shahi land retaken by Barha Tegin c. 665 and Bost is Rutbil's by 671 (the page has Rabi ibn Ziyad attack him there). The page gives no area, so the shape is Zabulistan plus the Arachosian strip of Cliopatria's Turk Shahis shape of 682.

correction.text: the part of Cliopatria's Turk Shahis shape of 692 that lies in Zabulistan and Arachosia: the Zunbils' kingdom

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 692-865: in Cliopatria the Zunbils are folded into the 'Turk Shahis' shape, whose 692 step adds 143 cells of Zabulistan and 348 of Arachosia (about 124,000 km2). The page has the kingdom 'between Zaranj in the southwest and Kabulistan in the northeast' reaching 'Rakhwad (al-Rukhkhaj) and Bost'; the Arab campaigns (698, c. 700, 711, 725-726, 769, c. 795) all met the Zunbils, not the Kabul Shahis.

correction.text: the Zabulistan and Arachosia part of Cliopatria's 866 shape, shrunk from the west by the Saffarids of Sistan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 866-870: Cliopatria thins the Zabulistan and Arachosia part (93 and 166 cells) before the Saffarid conquest; the page dates only 870 ('Yaqub bin Laith al-Saffar defeated the Zunbils and conquered their territory from Sistan'), so the thinning is kept as drawn at confidence 1.

ledger.note: 680: Rutbil founds the Zunbil kingdom at Ghazni and Zamindawar. 'In 680-683, Rutbil split from his brother, the Shahi of Kabul, per al-Tabari'; infobox 'From circa 680 AD until the Saffarid conquest in 870 AD'. Arab sources name Rutbil from 666 and have him resist Rabi ibn Ziyad at Bost in 671 and conclude the 673 peace.

region.text: Arachosia, 'as far as Kandahar', with Bost and Rakhwad

ledger.note: 692: the Zunbil kingdom reaches Kandahar. The page gives the reach ('Arachosia reached as far as Kandahar'; 'the southern reach at times included Rakhwad (al-Rukhkhaj) and Bost') but no date; 692 is Cliopatria's step. The Turk Shahi page has Barha Tegin retake 'territory as far as Arachosia and Kandahar' c. 665.

ledger.note: 870: Ya'qub ibn al-Layth destroys the Zunbils. '870: Yaqub bin Laith al-Saffar defeated the Zunbils and conquered their territory from Sistan'; '870/871: Yaqub's eastern campaign began, including the conquest of Ghazna'. The death of the last Zunbil is not on the page.

wars.name: Arab campaigns against the Zunbils
wars.outcome: Ibn Samura reached Zamindawar (653-654); Rabi ibn Ziyad drove Rutbil to al-Rukhkhaj (671); Ubayd Allah's 'Army of Destruction' was defeated and paid tribute (698); Ibn al-Ash'ath made terms c. 700 and rebelled; Qutayba forced tribute in 711. No annexation.
wars.note: Before 680 the opponent is Rutbil as the Turk Shahis' lieutenant or brother.

wars.name: Abbasid tribute campaigns against the Zunbils
wars.outcome: Yazid ibn al-Ghurayf failed to obtain tribute (725-726); Ma'n b. Za'ida defeated the Zunbils near Ghazni and got tribute (769); the Shah Bahar temple was destroyed c. 795; al-Ma'mun's 815 victory over the Kabul Shahis left the Zunbils 'unaffected'.

wars.name: Saffarid conquest of the Zunbils

zones.text: the part of Cliopatria's Turk Shahis shape of 692 that lies in Zabulistan and Arachosia: the Zunbils' kingdom

wars.outcome: Yaqub bin Laith al-Saffar conquered Zunbil territory from Sistan in 870 and took Ghazna in the eastern campaign of 870/871.
wars.note: The start year is Cliopatria's 866 thinning; the page dates only 870.

certainty.note: No border is drawn on the pages; the Zunbil frontier ('between Zaranj in the southwest and Kabulistan in the northeast') is a reach, not a line.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks (its land is folded into the 692-870 shapes of 'Turk Shahis'); written by sa-03-a because the Turk Shahis dossier removes it. Zunbils page only (plus the Turk Shahi page): no Zunbil rulers list is used (Rutbil, Shiquer/Zigil named; no dated succession). The infobox start 680 conflicts with Arab mentions of Rutbil from 666 and with the page's 'In 680-683' split date. The 720 Tang recognition of the Zunbil ruler Shiquer (Zigil) is a title, not a dated protectorate, and is left to the Tang group (no ledger event). The Arab campaigns 653-711 are in the war list only (the kingdom did not yet exist as a Cliopatria shape). Capitals have no years on the page. Wikidata unknown (the page was read, not Wikidata), so null. Saffarid dossier (me-08) should record the 870 gain with this dossier as counterpart.
